note: House style for generated exercise illustrations, decided 10 September 2026 after five rounds of samples: flat minimal illustrations with a small muted palette, generated by the cheapest image model at the smallest allowed size and low quality; SVG figure composition and photographs of people rejected; real photographs only for KNM items about real places, documents and objects. Every generated image is reviewed before use.
modelNote: Cheapest model in the comparison of 10 September 2026 (about 439 output tokens for 1024x1024 and 343 for 1536x1024 at $30 per million, roughly one cent per image as reported by the API; verify on the usage dashboard). gpt-image-2.5-sunburst is an equivalent fallback.
stylePrefix: Minimal flat illustration made of a few simple shapes: no outlines, no texture, no background objects. Palette: warm off-white paper, charcoal grey, mustard yellow, plus one or two muted colours used sparingly (dusty blue, sage green, soft terracotta). Large empty space, deliberately low detail, friendly and calm, everyday Netherlands. No text, no captions, no logos.
sequenceRule: Generate a three-picture task as one image with three equal panels separated by thin gaps, describing the same character with three fixed traits (hair, glasses or hat, jacket colour) in every panel; split the panels afterwards. Regenerate when a trait changes between panels.
pairRule: Generate a two-picture choice as two separate single images with the same style prefix; the two options must differ in the one thing the task asks about and match in everything else.
reviewChecklist: no readable text, signage or logos
hands, faces and objects without artefacts at the size the app shows the image
the answer-relevant detail is unambiguous (the flat tyre, the three items on the tray)
the character's fixed traits match across a sequence
nothing culturally or factually wrong for the Netherlands
alt text written in Dutch without revealing a key

cast.note: Recurring named characters for prompts and questions; describe them with the same three traits every time. Implied family links used across items: Fatima is the mother of Amina and Sem; Hasan is Sem's father; Roos appears as Amina's older sister in one picnic item. Keep new links consistent with these.
cast.Sem: teenage boy, short brown hair, green sweater
cast.Roos: young woman, dark hair in a bun, yellow scarf
cast.Karim: man in his thirties, short black hair and beard, grey jacket
cast.Fatima: woman in her forties, headscarf, blue coat
cast.meneer De Vries: man of about 60, grey hair, round glasses, dark blue jacket
cast.mevrouw Bakker: woman of about 65, short white hair, red cardigan
cast.Julio: young man, curly hair, striped shirt
cast.Amina: girl of about 10, two braids, purple hoodie
cast.Modibo: young man, short black hair, light shirt
cast.Sabrina: woman in her thirties, long dark hair, green jumper
cast.Hasan: man in his fifties, grey moustache, brown cap

sketchPrefix: Very simple line drawing with few thin lines, like a quick pen sketch in a notebook: only the essential people and objects, no background, no shading, no texture, soft slightly uneven pen line, large empty warm off-white space; mustard yellow used on exactly one object per panel. Deliberately low detail. No text, no captions, no logos.
sketchPrefixUse: optional alternative for picture notes in writing tasks, if chosen
qualityNote: For this flat style, low quality is indistinguishable from medium at display size and costs about a third (171 output tokens for 816x816, 107 for 1024x640 on 10 September 2026).
sizeNote: The API refuses anything under 655,360 pixels (640x640 was rejected); 816x816 and 1024x640 are the smallest practical sizes. Images are shown at about 500-600 px wide, so nothing larger is needed.

delivery.note: Serve at the generated width (1024 px landscape, 816 px square) as WebP; 600 px looked soft on high-density screens at the column width the app uses. Keep the generated PNG under content/images-source (ignored by git).

costPerImage.basis: API-reported output tokens at $30 per million; confirm on the usage dashboard

sequence: Generate a three-picture task as three separate images with the same style prefix, each brief repeating the character's three fixed traits verbatim and naming the same setting; check the traits across the three pictures at review and regenerate the panel whose trait drifted. (A single three-panel generation was the first plan; separate panels gave consistent characters for the batch 008 picture notes and split cleanly into the app's picture row.)
